notes.title: Changelog – Fight Prototype v0.26.5.9.02
notes.content:
[b]New Features[/b]

Finisher Move: Added a new finisher mechanic to the game, allowing for more impactful combat sequences.
Tutorial: Introduced a tutorial to guide players through core mechanics and gameplay basics.

[b]Visuals & Effects[/b]

Placeholder VFX: Basic visual effects have been implemented to enhance fight sequences (to be refined in future updates).
Camera Shake: Added camera shake feedback on player attacks to improve immersion.

notes.title: It’s Time to Change the Old Demo and Why (Part 1)
notes.content:
[p][/p][p][/p][p][b]Get a free Steam key when the game is fully released by participating in our new fight system playtest! 
[/b][/p][p][b]👉 Join our Discord:[/b] [/p][p][url="https://discord.gg/jwc5bq9CkN"]https://discord.gg/jwc5bq9CkN[/url] [/p][p][b]Important Note: The current demo will be unavailable starting August 17th, and it will be replaced by the new demo.[/b][/p][p][b]In past devlogs, we talked about our dream and the earlier prototypes that led to the current demo. We shared our vision, story, and challenges, but we never really discussed its gameplay mechanics, especially the fight system.[/b][/p][p][b]With a completely different new demo coming soon, it’s time to go back to the beginning and explain how we ended up with the current demo’s mechanics, and how these decisions will influence the upcoming demos.[/b][/p][p][b]From the start, we knew that in an [i]action-adventure[/i] game, the “action” part needed to have a real, meaningful impact on gameplay. So the first thing that came to mind was focusing on the fighting mechanics. We began with a simple, over-the-shoulder camera style, centered on the player, with a few basic combos and a simple parry system.[/b][/p][p][/p][h3][b]First fight system Video here:[/b][/h3][p][/p][previewyoutube="j9avL0TdbYU;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p][b]The system was simple yet functional. At that time, the idea was for close, one-on-one, personal fights, which also matched the overall gameplay vision we had. The original version was also supposed to include stealth mechanics. So while Soroush was busy working on the fight system, Ahmad was working on gameplay features and the stealth system.[/b][/p][p][b]For this, we needed a fully functional traversal system so the player could move vertically, crouch to hide from enemy patrols, and use other sub-mechanics to stay undetected.[/b][/p][p][b] [/b][/p][h3][b]First playable area video here:[/b][/h3][p][/p][previewyoutube="1UeHittoMAc;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p][b]But that didn’t stop us from refining the fight system. Soon, it was time to integrate the character model into the fight system, adding improved attack combos.[/b][/p][p][/p][h3][b]First implementation here:[/b][/h3][p][/p][previewyoutube="lTrjxJG-j6Y;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h3][b]The final result for the current demo’s fight system was this:[/b][/h3][p][/p][previewyoutube="VjC7SLfetT4;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p][b]With the fight system on track, it was time to refine the gameplay systems further. But simple mechanics weren’t enough for us. In addition to the traversal system, we gradually developed a more dynamic, directed camera system similar to older action games.[/b][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Watch both videos here:[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="Q79_KzRoS14;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="AyuodGuWBKo;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p][b]After the demo, everything started to change. One mechanic after another evolved, and with a mix of a new art style and our team’s growing capabilities, the game began transforming into something much bigger.[/b][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Prototypes, Dead Ends& How the Core Team Nearly Gave Up
notes.content:
[p][/p][p][b]👉 Join our Discord:  [/b][/p][p][url="https://discord.gg/jwc5bq9CkN"]https://discord.gg/jwc5bq9CkN[/url][/p][p][url="https://discord.gg/jwc5bq9CkN" style="button" buttoncolor="#03438c"]Discord [/url][/p][p]In those early months, [b]everything was trial and error[/b].
Prototypes. Sketches. Scrapped builds. Endless experimentation with mechanics and ideas. The process was frustratingly slow, but it was a messy, chaotic journey to discover Firva’s true heart.[/p][p]Without a full team, all we could do was build simple prototypes. But even the best prototype is just a shell unless it has a story worth telling.[/p][p]We wrestled with the same big questions every developer faces:[/p][list][*][p][i]Does the story grow from the gameplay, or should the gameplay grow from the story?[/i][/p][/*][*][p][i]What about the market? What kind of stories are acceptable or wanted?[/i][/p][/*][*][p][i]How would we even publish this thing?[/i][/p][/*][/list][p]It was these late-night questions, echoing in our minds, that slowly shaped our thinking and ultimately led us to create the first [b]Firva[/b] demo.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]After Taliman: Clarity, But Still No Heart[/b][/p][p]After the Taliman, the team finally had a clearer vision of what Firva could be, but we still lacked a core narrative, the “why” behind the game.[/p][p][b]Reza[/b] knew what kind of story he wanted to tell: a dark fantasy, something bold and memorable. But how to actually tell that story remained a mystery.[/p][p]In the final days of Taliman, our team grew by two:[/p][list][*][p][b]Ahmad Talayi[/b] (Technical Artist)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Mohammad Shahabi[/b] (Writer)[/p][/*][/list][p]Mohammad, stepping in as our writer, was handed a stack of scripts from previous freelance writers. But he was determined to create a dark fantasy world that was entirely ours, infusing Firva with his own ideas and voice.[/p][p]Ahmad, meanwhile, began as a technical artist but quickly became the creator behind many of Firva’s most iconic set pieces.[/p][p]With the expanded team, everything seemed possible.
Here’s how we were shaping up:[/p][list][*][p][b]Reza[/b] – Project Lead[/p][/*][*][p][b]Sorush[/b] – Lead Developer & Programmer[/p][/*][*][p][b]Ahmad[/b] – Technical Artist[/p][/*][*][p][b]Peyman[/b] – Art Lead[/p][/*][*][p][b]Mohammad[/b] – Writer[/p][/*][/list][p]With only a handful of team members and even fewer resources, we made a pact to focus on one thing:
[b]Making something tangible.[/b]
A concept demo, something we could actually share with others.[/p][p] [/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="vvtO0mPknBQ;full"][/previewyoutube][p] [/p][p]But just as we were gaining momentum, disaster struck.
[b]Peyman[/b], our Art Lead, the person responsible for Firva’s unique visual style, decided to leave. His departure was understandable. He wasn’t satisfied with the pace of progress, and with Reza also busy with other projects, Peyman felt the time was right to step away. So, in August 2022, he left the team.[/p][p]For a moment, it felt like this could be the death of the project. Peyman had given Firva its distinctive look. The demo we’d been preparing was built around his vision.[/p][p]After his sudden departure, we were left with a choice: surrender or push forward.
We chose to continue.[/p][p]We still had a story, we still had art assets Peyman had created, and most importantly, we still had the will to keep going.[/p][p]This was a turning point. The team made a bold decision:
[b]Lean fully into the cinematic aspect, finish the demo, and push for its release.[/b][/p][p][b]Soroush[/b] stepped up to take on the role of Project Lead.
[b]Mohammad[/b] became the Director, guiding the narrative vision.
[b]Ahmad[/b] took the helm for development, pulling together everything we had.[/p][p]Together, we finished what we’d started.[/p][p]And finally, we released the first public demo for Firva.[/p][p] [/p][p] [/p][previewyoutube="YrNpNmRk-wo;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]Looking back, the journey through prototypes, setbacks, and changes in the team wasn’t wasted effort.
Every dead end taught us something. Every frustration pushed us to ask deeper questions about what Firva could be.[/p][p]And in the end, it was perseverance [b]the decision to keep going[/b] that helped us find Firva’s true heart.[/p]

notes.title: The Untold Origins of Firva
notes.content: [h1]How It All Began: [/h1][p][/p][p]Every story has its humble beginnings, and Firva is no different. But what makes our story unique is that it didn’t start with a big budget, a fancy studio, or even a clear roadmap. It began with something far more powerful: a dream. A dream driven by ambition, determination, and a passion to create something meaningful.[/p][p]Firva was born from the vision of our project lead, Reza Sajjady. He didn’t want to make just another game. No, he envisioned a dark world, a narrative-driven world, where cinematic flair met impactful gameplay. It wasn’t just about fun; it was about crafting a story worth telling. But like any creative project, the hardest part wasn’t the vision itself; it was finding the right story to bring to life.[/p][p]The journey started small, with just Reza’s vision and a blank slate. But Reza knew that to bring his dream to reality, he needed help. In March 2021, Soroush Hosseinpour joined the team. As the first addition to the project, Soroush played a pivotal role, starting with prototypes. And after months of trial and error, by the end of September, they created “Alex,” the first prototype.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="9QTyH5x6ueg;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]It was rudimentary. Some might argue it wasn’t even a true prototype yet. But for us, it was a milestone. It was the first tangible proof that they were on the right track.[/p][p]But one prototype wasn’t enough. With only two people on the team, the scope of the project quickly became clear: you can’t make a complex, narrative-driven game with only two people and limited resources. The next 12 months were spent experimenting, iterating, and testing, creating a lot of ideas but not much to show for it. They struggled. Progress was slow, and at times, the dream felt far out of reach. Yet they never gave up. Even as the prototypes piled up, they were slowly discovering the heart of Firva, piece by piece.[/p][p]After a year of experimentation, the team still wasn’t anywhere near where they wanted to be. The process had been messy, full of setbacks, but also learning. It was clear they needed more than just ideas; they needed people. That’s when Peyman came into the picture.[/p][p]With Peyman on board, the team felt reinvigorated. In just six months, they were able to bring more structure to their work, building a more polished and cohesive version of the game, which we now call Taliman. It wasn’t the finished product, but it was the best they’d created so far.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="ozNslSkganE;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]But even after 24 months of testing and prototyping, the team still felt like they were starting over. They had come a long way, but they were far from their original vision. By March 2023, they were back at square one, rethinking their approach, revisiting old ideas, and reimagining what Firva could truly become.[/p][p]The Core Never Gave Up[/p][p]Through all of the ups and downs, Firva was always driven by a singular idea: to create something meaningful. It was never easy, and often it felt like they were getting nowhere. But slowly, piece by piece, Firva began to take shape. They were never alone in the struggle, though. Over the years, talented people came and went, leaving their mark on the project. And though many of them moved on, the core of the team, Reza, Soroush, and Peyman, never gave up.[/p][p]Today, Firva is far from finished, but the journey has been as important as the destination. From humble beginnings to the prototype that barely existed, to Taliman, and now to the next chapter, Firva is a game that was made not by a big budget, but by passion, perseverance, and the dream of telling a story that matters.[/p][p]And we’re just getting started.[/p][p]Next time we are going to write about the current Steam Demo, so stay tuned[/p][p]Thank you for sticking with us. Let’s begin again. This time together[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]👉 Join our Discord:  [/p][p][/p][p][url="https://discord.gg/jwc5bq9CkN"]https://discord.gg/jwc5bq9CkN[/url][/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Are We Dead?
notes.content:
[h1][b]Devlog 001:
[/b][/h1][h3]The Harsh Truth of Indie Development[/h3][p]If you’ve been around Steam long enough, you’ve seen it:
A promising indie game appears a striking trailer, a cool-looking demo. You wishlist it, maybe even follow the Devs, hoping this is one of those rare gems that makes it.[/p][p]And then… silence.[/p][p]No updates. No Devlogs. No social posts. It starts to feel familiar. Another project, another good idea, gone. Swallowed by the same uncertainties that haunt indie games everywhere.[/p][p]As gamers ourselves, we know that feeling all too well. We’ve clicked Wishlist on those same projects, wondered [i]what if[/i]. Even when the demo is rough, unfinished, or broken, you still imagine the potential. The version that could’ve been, the game that never made it.[/p][p]It’s easy to assume the worst.
“They must have quit.”
“Maybe the hype wasn’t enough.”
“It probably got abandoned.”[/p][p]We’ve been there. We’ve thought the same things. That’s why this post matters.[/p][p][b]So… Are We Dead?[/b][/p][p]No. We’re not dead. But after 15 months of near silence, we owe you an explanation.[/p][p]Firva is not abandoned. After all it was our beloved creation.[/p][p]It has changed maybe a lot that what you expect even more than what we could have hoped

[/p][p]When we started building [b]Firva[/b] a cinematic, story-driven fantasy game about intertwined destinies we had no idea where the journey would lead. Like countless teams before us, we dove in with nothing but passion, a dream, and that foolish indie optimism.[/p][p]But dreams collide with reality.
Resources run thin.
Life gets messy.
And in our case, life got really messy.[/p][p][b]Team changes. Endless obstacles.[/b][/p][p]And yet… we’re still here.[/p][p]Today marks the start of our weekly Devlog series an honest, behind-the-scenes look at how we’ve fought to keep Firva alive, and how it’s evolved for better or worse.[/p][p]We’ll talk about:[/p][list][*][p]How this all began: The vision, the first prototypes, and all the versions you never saw.[/p][/*][*][p]Why this game matters to us. The gaps we saw in the genre. The unique story we felt had to be told.[/p][/*][*][p]Our core pillars: Cinematic storytelling. Tight, impactful combat. Deep world-building.[/p][/*][*][p]How the team has grown and sometimes shrunk. The hard lessons learned along the way.[/p][/*][/list][p]This is our story a story built between setbacks, through uncertainty, written in the margins of chaos.[/p][p]We’re not dead. We’ve been quietly rebuilding. And now, we’re ready to show you where Firva stands.[/p][p][b]Thank you for sticking with us. Let’s begin again. This time together[/b][/p][p][/p][p]👉 Join our Discord:  [/p][p][url="https://discord.gg/jwc5bq9CkN"]https://discord.gg/jwc5bq9CkN[/url][/p][p][/p][p][/p]
